name: HivePunk 1071
subject: Microcks v2
thesis: Microcks v2 is an early discussion rather than a committed release plan, with 1.16.0 as the current stable context. The conclusion is cautious: the direction is constrained by compatibility and simplicity principles, but the technical-foundation choices remain open.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: microcks/microcks has 18 raw commits in the last 30 days, 11 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is 6546fe9, on 2026-11-12.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Microcks is described as a CNCF incubating project and an open source, cloud native tool for API Mocking and Testing.
claims.quote: The open source, cloud native tool for API Mocking and Testing. Microcks is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation incubating project 🚀

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Microcks turns OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, gRPC protobuf, GraphQL, Postman and SoapUI assets into live mocks and reuses them for contract and non-regression tests.
claims.quote: Mocking & Testing Microcks is a platform for turning your API and microservices assets - OpenAPI specs , AsyncAPI specs , gRPC protobuf , GraphQL schema , Postman collections , SoapUI projects - into live mocks in seconds.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Issue #2412 was opened on Nov 3, 2026 and is open.
claims.missing: Its source holds no passage that says this.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #2412 says nothing is decided unless explicitly stated and presents early ideas, trade-offs and open questions.
claims.quote: What follows is the state of an early study. Nothing is decided unless explicitly stated : these are ideas, trade-offs and open questions, grouped by theme.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The guiding principles include keeping the API contract as source of truth, preserving backward compatibility especially for the CLI, keeping new capabilities opt-in, and keeping the Uber distribution simple and lightweight.
claims.quote: A few guiding principles for the discussion: The API contract remains the source of truth for mocks and tests.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: For the database study, MongoDB 4.4 in compose files is end-of-life, and 5.0 and 6.0 are also described as end-of-life.
claims.quote: 🔎 MongoDB 4.4 (used in our compose files) is end-of-life; 5.0 and 6.0 as well.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The study lists target MongoDB version and AVX CPU requirement, embedded database for Uber, CNCF SSPL position, 4.4 upgrade notes, and DocumentDB as open points.
claims.quote: Technical foundation Database: keep MongoDB, on a recent version 🔎 MongoDB 4.4 (used in our compose files) is end-of-life; 5.0 and 6.0 as well.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The Quarkus study is motivated by Spring Boot weight and OpenTelemetry setup pain, faster startup, lower memory, native builds, and a single stack.
claims.quote: 🔎 Motivations: Spring Boot feels heavy, OpenTelemetry was painful to set up during the Spring Boot 4 migration, the async minion already runs on Quarkus, and it opens the door to faster startup, lower memory, native builds and a single stack.

risks: Issue #2412 states nothing is decided unless explicitly stated, so 2.0 scope remains uncertain.
MongoDB 4.4 is described as end-of-life, with 5.0 and 6.0 also described as end-of-life, requiring a version decision.
The MongoDB SSPL licence and CNCF position are listed as to be confirmed, not settled.
A PostgreSQL/JSONB alternative is described as a large rewrite and migration effort.
The Spring Boot to Quarkus move is described as strong coupling concentrated in servlet mock processing, Mongo persistence, and security, so it is not purely mechanical.
unknowns: Issue #2412 was opened on Nov 3, 2026 and is open.: Its source holds no passage that says this.

Whether Microcks 2.0 will ship, and on what date, is not stated in the pages read.: A decided roadmap, release plan, or statement in issue #2412 or project documentation confirming 2.0 scope and timing.
wouldChangeMind: A decided statement in issue #2412 choosing the database and web framework for 2.0.
A public 2.0 roadmap or release target replacing the current early-study framing.
Evidence that the CLI compatibility or Uber simplicity principles have been changed.
